newsitem.title: UK: World insurance premiums over $2 trillion - report.
newsitem.headline: World insurance premiums over $2 trillion - report.

text.p: World insurance premiums have broken through the $2 trillion mark for the first time, but while Asia is booming, growth in Europe and America has fallen off, reinsurers Swiss Re said Friday.
In its latest Sigma research report, Swiss Re said insurance premium volume in 1995 was $2.14 trillion, an increase of 3.7 percent over the previous year.
"This indicated growth which, like the previous year, was below the long-term average of 4.6 percent," the report said.
In a sluggish year, non-life insurance achieved revenues of $906.8 billion, up 2.2 percent, mostly from Europe and the United States.
Life insurance counted for $1.24 trillion, up 5.3 percent, reaching highs in Japan and South Korea, South Africa and Switzerland.
In the United States, falling prices in non-life insurance led to weak growth, while in life insurance, below-average to negative growth was recorded for individual products.
